operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole operative sentence of Executive Order 8304 revokes Executive Order No. 2552 of March 21, 1917, which withdrew public land in Alaska for lighthouse purposes; its operative words are 'is hereby revoked'. A present-tense revocation with no later effective date is carried out when the order takes effect, so the command was exhausted by performance on the order's signing date, 1939-12-19, which is recorded as the end. The filing date December 20, 1939 and the issue date December 22, 1939 are the alternatives if effectiveness is dated from filing or publication. The Federal Register docket line reads 'Filed, December 20, 1939;' and the issue is headed 'Washington, Friday, December 22, 1939'.

research_rationale:
Identity and text: the held original is the machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register issue (4 FR 4909, PDF pages 1-1, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-1939-12-22/pdf/FR-1939-12-22.pdf, sha256 219867f10645ab4bfd1ade1aec42fbd1234152da7b31967961625065186d7f4d); the text layer is OCR, the page image is not held in the repository, and the order was identified from the text layer. The order's heading, subject, signature date and closing number tag appear together as one short order whose whole text is the clause. Inventory: one operative sentence revoking Executive Order No. 2552 of March 21, 1917, which withdrew public land in Alaska for lighthouse purposes; there is no other clause. End: a present-tense revocation is carried out when the order takes effect, and the order postpones nothing, so the command was exhausted by performance on its signing date 1939-12-19; the filing date December 20, 1939 and the issue date December 22, 1939 are the alternative dates if effectiveness is dated from filing or publication. The packet's one machine lead for a later instrument is Executive Order 10287 of September 6, 1951. Its held heading cites the number 8304 with the date January 14, 1939, which does not match this order (signed December 19, 1939), and its body revokes a different order, number 8034 of January 14, 1939, and abolishes the Federal Real Estate Board. It does not revoke or name this order and is rejected as a lead. Later instruments: the packet's later-events search of Office of the Federal Register disposition notes (1937 onward) and its current-law searches of the U.S. Code and the eCFR were selected after reading their coverage notes, and each returned no hit for this order. A later revocation or repeal of the order is not needed to end a command that was already performed.

The one lead naming a later instrument (Executive Order 10287 of 1951) does not revoke or name this order, as stated in the rationale.","independent_command_check":"The order holds one command, the revocation of the earlier order named in it; no report, delegation, rule or second command appears in the held text.","savings_check":"The held text has no savings clause; the only residual is the completed revocation, recorded as an accrued consequence.","scope_check":"The whole order is a single clause with no partial, conditional or severable part, and no amendment to its text is held."}

savings_residuals.reason: The held text contains no savings or transition clause. Its single command, revocation of Executive Order No. 2552 of March 21, 1917, which withdrew public land in Alaska for lighthouse purposes, was completed when the order took effect. The revoked order's loss of effect is a completed consequence that survives as an accrued result, not as a continuing command of this order.

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Gerrit S. Miller, Jr., Curator of Mammals in the United States National Museum, Smithsonian Institution, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The operative paragraph of Executive Order 8340 exempts Frank E. Gass from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, for a term it states as 'for a period of one year ending February 28, 1941'. The exemption is a fixed-term command, so it ends by its own terms on the stated date, 1941-02-28. The date is recorded inclusive, as the exemption runs through the end of February 28, 1941; the exclusive reading, under which the term ends when that day begins, is the alternative. The grant is personal to one named person and nothing in the held text makes it depend on a report, an event or a later order.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Frank E. Gass, correspondence clerk, Bureau of International Exchanges, Smithsonian Institution, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Frank E. Gass from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending February 28, 1941.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

source.page_or_item: Executive Order 8345—Exemption of Fred C. Bailey From Compulsory Retirement for Age; February 12, 1940; APP node 210214; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T05:38:46Z
source.quote: Bailey from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending March 31, 1941.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The operative paragraph of Executive Order 8345 further exempts Fred C. Bailey from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, for a term it states as 'for a period of one year ending March 31, 1941'. The exemption is a fixed-term command, so it ends by its own terms on the stated date, 1941-03-31. The date is recorded inclusive, as the exemption runs through the end of March 31, 1941; the exclusive reading, under which the term ends when that day begins, is the alternative. The grant is personal to one named person and nothing in the held text makes it depend on a report, an event or a later order. The recital cites the earlier exemption order Executive Order 8060 of March 7, 1939 as predecessor; it precedes this order and are not events affecting it.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Fred C. Bailey, Fleet Manager, Maintenance and Repair Division, United States Maritime Commission, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending March 31, 1940, by Executive Order No. 8060 of March 7, 1939, be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby further exempt the said Fred C. Bailey from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending March 31, 1941.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

Under the authority vested in me by 
section 1  (b) of Part I  of Reorganization 
Plan No. I I 1  (effective July 1, 1939, by 
Public Resolution approved June 7, 1939, 
53 Stat. 1431), and in effectuation of the

scribed in paragraph 1  hereof and shall

Under the authority vested in me by 
section 1  (b) of Part I  of Reorganization 
Plan No. I I 1  (effective July 1, 1939, by 
Public Resolution approved June 7, 1939, 
53 Stat. 1431), and in effectuation of the 
provisions of subdivisions (2), (3), and 
(4) of that section, I  hereby prescribe
the following regulations pertaining to 
officers designated by the Secretary of 
Commerce and the Secretary of Agricul­
ture under the said subdivisions:
1. Officers designated by the Secretary 
of Commerce and the Secretary of Agri­
culture under subdivisions (2) and (3), 
respectively, of the said section 1  (b) of 
Part I  of Reorganization Plan No. H 
may, when acceptable to the Secretary 
of State, be sent abroad as specialists or 
technicians for temporary service under 
the provisions of, and subject to the con­
ditions named in, section 5 of the act of 
March 3, 1927, 44 Stat. 1396, and section 
2 of the act of June 5, 1930, 46 Stat. 498, 
as authorized by the said subdivisions
(2) and (3), respectively.
2. The Secretary of State shall give 
suitable commissions to the officers de­
scribed in paragraph 1  hereof and shall 
assign them to such offices as may be 
deemed necessary by him and the Secre­
tary of the department concerned. 
Such officers, during the active period 
of their assignment, shall be considered 
a part of the organization of the Foreign 
Service, shall assume the status directed 
by the Secretary of State, and shall, in 
this respect, be subject to the juris­
diction of the Secretary of State. With 
the approval of the chief of the office 
to which they are attached, such officers 
may request reports from Foreign Ser­
vice officers upon matters falling within 
the jurisdiction of their respective de­
partments. The duties of such officers 
shall be restricted to the accomplish­
ment of the special missions within the 
scope of their assignments.
3. The officers designated by the Sec­
retary of Commerce and the Secretary 
of Agriculture under subdivision (4) of 
the said section 1  (b) of Part I of Re­
organization Plan No. II to serve in the 
Department of State as liaison officers 
shall, when acceptable to the Secretary 
of State, serve in matters of interest to 
their respective departments.

Later instruments: the packet's later-events search of Office of the Federal Register disposition notes (1937 onward) and its current-law searches of the U.S. Code and the eCFR were selected after reading their coverage notes, and each returned no hit for this order. Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Louis A. Simon, supervising architect of the Public Buildings Administration, Federal Works Agency, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for periods totaling three years by Executive Orders No. 7581 of March 19, 1937, No. 7824 of February 25, 1938, and No. 8046 of February 11, 1939, be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby further exempt the said Louis A. Simon from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending May 31, 1941.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

The White House,

March 7, 1940.

source.quote: Johnson from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending May 31, 1941.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The operative paragraph of Executive Order 8391 exempts Clifton E. Johnson from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, for a term it states as 'for a period of one year ending May 31, 1941'. The exemption is a fixed-term command, so it ends by its own terms on the stated date, 1941-05-31. The date is recorded inclusive, as the exemption runs through the end of May 31, 1941; the exclusive reading, under which the term ends when that day begins, is the alternative. The grant is personal to one named person and nothing in the held text makes it depend on a report, an event or a later order.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Clifton E. Johnson, senior mechanic, United States Coast Guard, Treasury Department, who, during the month of May, 1940, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Clifton E. Johnson from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending May 31, 1941.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The operative paragraph of Executive Order 8412 exempts Charles M. Eichelberger from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, for a term it states as 'for a period of one year ending June 30, 1941'. The exemption is a fixed-term command, so it ends by its own terms on the stated date, 1941-06-30. The date is recorded inclusive, as the exemption runs through the end of June 30, 1941; the exclusive reading, under which the term ends when that day begins, is the alternative. The grant is personal to one named person and nothing in the held text makes it depend on a report, an event or a later order.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Charles M. Eichelberger, Chief Accountant and Auditor, Compensation Board, Navy Department, who, during the month of June, 1940, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, see. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Charles M. Eichelberger from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending June 30, 1941.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT
